title: BMA executor bma-file types
description: fs.mount and fs.unmount (machine-scoped executors with the fs capability). bma-file HTTP routes live under the service_url the harness sends (a complete prefix ending in /v1/machines/{machine_id}/fs, for example https://executor.example.com/v1/machines/mach_01/fs, operations at <service_url>/<op>; the executor does not compose the machine id); they are authenticated with the mount token, not executor methods. Read routes (contract 1.18.0 writes them down; they are what FUSE and an fs.copy_views copy use), every one with "Authorization: Bearer <token>": POST <service_url>/list, body {view, path, after?, limit?} -> {data: FsEntry[], has_more, last_id?}, the entries of a directory sorted by name, at most limit (default 1000, at most 5000) after the name after, the next page passes after = last_id; POST <service_url>/lookup, body {view, path} -> {entry: FsEntry}; GET <service_url>/read?view=&path= with optional Range: bytes=a-b -> the bytes, 206 with Content-Range whenever less than the whole file is returned (also without Range: one answer carries at most 8 MiB, so read on from the next offset), 416 for a range starting at or past the end, header X-Bma-File-Digest: sha256:<hex of the whole file>. path is absolute inside the view (/ is the view root; skills: /<skill name>/<file>). Errors are the platform error envelope {error: {code, message}}: 401 token_expired, invalid_token or token_revoked (do not retry with that token; wait for the next fs.mount), 403 view_not_granted, 404 not_found or content_missing, 400 invalid_path, not_a_directory, is_a_directory or invalid_range; 429 and 5xx may be retried. Writes (PUT /files, POST /rename|unlink|mkdir|rmdir|setattr) answer 403 workspace_read_only on read-only views.

FsEntry.description: Contract 1.18.0. One node of a view as the bma-file list and lookup routes describe it. mode is the permission bits (0o555 directories and executable files, 0o444 other files; views are read-only), mtime Unix seconds (0 when unknown), sha256 the lower-case hex digest of a file's whole content (absent for directories).

FsMount.description: One view to mount. path is the absolute mount point on the executor host (derived from session_files by the harness; the skills view is at <root>/<agent_session_id>/skills for an executor that declared fs.skills_per_session or fs.copy_views, and is not mounted for any other executor). For a view the executor declared in fs.copy_views, "mount" means: copy the view's files to path as read-only files (see FsCapability.copy_views). Mount points of different sessions never overlap, and the executor mounts exactly the path it is given. readonly is also fixed inside token; the executor mounts read-only when it is true. token is a capability token for this session and machine: keep it in memory only, never write it to disk, argv, environment or logs.

view.description: uploads, skills. Open enum: outputs and memory follow.

options.description: Reserved mount tuning (string values); unknown keys are ignored.

FsMountResult.description: fs.mount result. state is "mounted" once every listed view is mounted and serving, or "failed" with error_code and error (nothing stays half-mounted).

SessionFilesFlushResult.description: session_files.flush result. state flushed: every changed output was uploaded; failed: at least one upload failed (error names it) and the request may be repeated.

FsUnmountResult.description: fs.unmount result. pending_bytes is data not yet committed to bma-file when flush was requested (always 0 for read-only views).
